### (a) Shear Force and Bending Moment Diagrams
**1. Support Reactions:**
Let the supports be $A$ ($x = 0$) and $B$ ($x = 6\text{ m}$). A point load of $50\text{ kN}$ acts at $C$ ($x = 2\text{ m}$), and a uniformly distributed load (UDL) of $20\text{ kN/m}$ acts from $D$ to $B$ ($x = 4\text{ m}$ to $x = 6\text{ m}$, span length = $2\text{ m}$). Let the roller support $B$ be at $x = 6\text{ m}$ and hinge $A$ at $x = 0$ (based on standard beam convention, noting position of roller at $2\text{ m}$ from right end, i.e., $x = 4\text{ m}$. Let us re-verify coordinates from diagram: Total length = $6\text{ m}$, spans are $2\text{ m} + 2\text{ m} + 2\text{ m}$. Support $A$ is at $x = 0$, roller support is at $x = 4\text{ m}$).  
Taking moments about $A$ ($R_B$ is at $x = 4\text{ m}$):  
$$\sum M_A = 0 \implies R_B(4) - 50(2) - (20 \times 2)\left(4 + \frac{2}{2}\right) = 0$$
$$4 R_B = 100 + (40 \times 5) = 100 + 200 = 300 \implies R_B = 75\text{ kN}$$
$$\sum F_y = 0 \implies R_A + R_B - 50 - (20 \times 2) = 0$$
$$R_A + 75 - 50 - 40 = 0 \implies R_A = 15\text{ kN}$$

**2. Shear Force (SF) Calculations:**
* Just right of $A$ ($x = 0^+$): $V = +15\text{ kN}$
* At $C$ ($x = 2^-$): $V = +15\text{ kN}$
* Just right of $C$ ($x = 2^+$): $V = 15 - 50 = -35\text{ kN}$
* At roller support ($x = 4^-$): $V = -35\text{ kN}$
* Just right of roller support ($x = 4^+$): $V = -35 + 75 = +40\text{ kN}$
* At $B$ ($x = 6^-$): $V = 40 - (20 \times 2) = 0$

**3. Bending Moment (BM) Calculations:**
* At $A$ ($x = 0$): $M = 0$
* At $C$ ($x = 2\text{ m}$): $M = 15 \times 2 = 30\text{ kN}\,\text{m}$
* At roller ($x = 4\text{ m}$): $M = 15(4) - 50(4 - 2) = 60 - 100 = -40\text{ kN}\,\text{m}$
* At free end $B$ ($x = 6\text{ m}$): $M = 0$

### (b) Maximum Absolute Values
* **Maximum Absolute Shear Force:** $|V|_{\max} = 40\text{ kN}$ (just to the right of the roller support).
* **Maximum Absolute Bending Moment:** $|M|_{\max} = 40\text{ kN}\,\text{m}$ (at the roller support location, $x = 4\text{ m}$).
proTip: Always double-check equilibrium equations ($\sum F_y = 0$ and $\sum M = 0$) before plotting SFD and BMD.
